name: CALCULATE
description_short: Evaluates an expression in a modified filter context.

params.name: filter1
params.description: A filter expression or table expression to apply

notes: Triggers context transition when used within a row context
Filters can be boolean expressions or FILTER/ALL table expressions
pitfalls: Context transition inside iterators may cause unexpected results
Boolean filter arguments overwrite existing filters on the same column

name: CALCULATETABLE
description_short: Evaluates a table expression in a modified filter context.
notes: Table equivalent of CALCULATE
Useful for passing filtered tables to other functions
pitfalls: Same context transition behavior as CALCULATE

name: FILTER
description_short: Returns a table that represents a subset of another table or expression.

params.name: filterExpression
params.description: A Boolean expression evaluated for each row

notes: Iterates row-by-row, so performance depends on table size
Can be used as a filter argument in CALCULATE
pitfalls: FILTER(ALL(FactTable), ...) can be very slow on large tables
Using FILTER when a simple boolean filter in CALCULATE would suffice

name: ALL
description_short: Returns all rows in a table, or all values in a column, ignoring any filters.
notes: Removes all filters from the specified table or columns
Used inside CALCULATE to remove context
pitfalls: ALL() on a table removes filters on all columns including related tables via relationships
Consider REMOVEFILTERS as a more readable alternative

name: ALLEXCEPT
description_short: Removes all context filters except those on the specified columns.

params.name: table
params.description: The table to remove filters from

params.name: column1
params.description: A column to keep filters on

notes: Shorthand for ALL with selective filter preservation
Also removes filters on related tables
pitfalls: Removes filters on columns from related tables too, unlike a combination of REMOVEFILTERS

name: VALUES
description_short: Returns a one-column table of distinct values, respecting filters. Adds blank row if present.
notes: Includes the blank row if there are missing values from relationships
In a scalar context, returns the single value if only one exists
pitfalls: Returns blank row unlike DISTINCT which excludes it
Use HASONEVALUE to check before converting to scalar

name: KEEPFILTERS
description_short: Modifies how filters are applied in CALCULATE, intersecting instead of overwriting.
notes: Without KEEPFILTERS, CALCULATE filters overwrite existing column filters
With KEEPFILTERS, the new filter intersects with existing filters
pitfalls: Can produce unexpected empty results if the intersection is empty

name: REMOVEFILTERS
description_short: Clears filters from specified tables or columns. A more readable alternative to ALL as a CALCULATE modifier.

params.name: table/column
params.description: Optional table or columns to clear filters from

notes: Semantically identical to ALL when used inside CALCULATE
More readable and explicit about intent
pitfalls: Without arguments, removes ALL filters in the entire model

name: TREATAS
description_short: Applies the result of a table expression as filters to columns in an unrelated table.

params.name: column1
params.description: Target column to apply filter to

notes: Creates a virtual relationship between tables
More performant than INTERSECT/FILTER combinations
pitfalls: Column data types must match between source and target

name: SUM
description_short: Adds all the numbers in a column.

params.name: column
params.description: The column containing numbers to sum

notes: Only works with column references, not expressions
For expressions, use SUMX
pitfalls: Cannot use SUM with calculated expressions; use SUMX instead

name: SUMX
description_short: Returns the sum of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function - evaluates expression row by row
Creates a row context for the expression
pitfalls: Performance can degrade on very large tables
Be aware of context transition if using CALCULATE inside the expression

name: AVERAGE
description_short: Returns the average (arithmetic mean) of all numbers in a column.
notes: Ignores blank values
Only works with column references
pitfalls: Blanks are excluded from the count, which may differ from expected behavior

name: AVERAGEX
description_short: Calculates the average of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function, similar to SUMX but computes average
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded from the average

name: COUNT
description_short: Counts the number of rows that contain non-blank values in a column.

params.name: column
params.description: Column to count non-blank values in

notes: Only counts non-blank values
For counting all rows including blanks, use COUNTROWS
pitfalls: Does not count blank values; use COUNTA for text columns

name: COUNTROWS
description_short: Counts the number of rows in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table to count rows in

notes: Counts all rows including those with blank values
Works with any table expression
pitfalls: Returns blank (not 0) if the table is empty

name: DISTINCTCOUNT
description_short: Counts the number of distinct values in a column.

params.name: column
params.description: Column to count distinct values in

notes: Includes blank as a distinct value if present
Equivalent to COUNTROWS(DISTINCT(column))
pitfalls: Counts blank as a value, which may inflate count by 1

name: MAX
description_short: Returns the largest value in a column or between two scalar expressions.
notes: With two arguments, works like a scalar MAX comparison
Ignores blank values
pitfalls: Two-argument form is scalar only, not row-by-row

name: MAXX
description_short: Returns the largest value of an expression evaluated for each row.
notes: Iterator function, useful for finding max of calculated values
pitfalls: Performance depends on table size

name: MIN
description_short: Returns the smallest value in a column or between two scalar expressions.
notes: Ignores blank values
Two-argument form is scalar comparison

name: MINX
description_short: Returns the smallest value of an expression evaluated for each row.
notes: Iterator function

name: RANKX
description_short: Returns the ranking of a number in a list of numbers for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: Table defining the list to rank against

params.name: expression
params.description: Expression evaluated for each row to create ranking list

params.name: value
params.description: The value to find rank for (optional, defaults to expression in current context)

notes: Commonly used in calculated columns and with ALL() in the table argument
pitfalls: Expensive on large tables
Context transition can affect results unexpectedly

name: IF
description_short: Checks a condition and returns one of two values.

params.name: logicalTest
params.description: A value or expression that returns TRUE or FALSE

params.name: resultIfTrue
params.description: Value returned when condition is TRUE

params.name: resultIfFalse
params.description: Value returned when condition is FALSE (default: BLANK())

notes: Third parameter is optional; defaults to BLANK()
Consider SWITCH for multiple conditions
pitfalls: Deeply nested IFs are hard to read; use SWITCH(TRUE(), ...) instead
Both branches may be evaluated for type checking

name: SWITCH
description_short: Evaluates an expression against a list of values and returns the corresponding result.
notes: Use SWITCH(TRUE(), ...) for multiple conditions as an IF replacement
More readable than nested IFs
pitfalls: All result expressions must return the same data type

name: AND
description_short: Checks whether both arguments are TRUE.
notes: Can also use && operator as shorthand
Only accepts two arguments; nest for more
pitfalls: For more than two conditions, use && operator which chains naturally

name: OR
description_short: Checks whether one of the arguments is TRUE.
notes: Can also use || operator as shorthand

name: NOT
description_short: Changes FALSE to TRUE, or TRUE to FALSE.

params.name: logical
params.description: A value or expression that returns a Boolean

name: COALESCE
description_short: Returns the first expression that does not evaluate to BLANK.
notes: Accepts any number of arguments
More concise than nested IF(ISBLANK(...), ..., ...)
pitfalls: All expressions must be of compatible types

name: DIVIDE
description_short: Performs division and returns alternate result on division by zero.

params.name: alternateResult
params.description: Value returned when divisor is 0 (default: BLANK())

notes: Safe division: avoids division by zero errors
Preferred over the / operator
pitfalls: Third parameter defaults to BLANK(), not 0

name: ROUND
description_short: Rounds a number to the specified number of digits.
notes: Negative numDigits rounds to the left of the decimal

name: ABS
description_short: Returns the absolute value of a number.

params.name: number
params.description: The number to get absolute value of

name: INT
description_short: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer.
notes: Always rounds towards negative infinity
pitfalls: INT(-1.5) returns -2, not -1

name: RELATED
description_short: Returns a related value from another table using an existing relationship.

params.name: column
params.description: A column from a related table

notes: Follows many-to-one relationships
Requires an active relationship between tables
pitfalls: Only works in row context (calculated columns or iterators)
Cannot traverse one-to-many; use RELATEDTABLE instead

name: RELATEDTABLE
description_short: Returns a table of rows related to the current row via relationships.
notes: Follows one-to-many relationships
Equivalent to CALCULATETABLE(<table>) in row context
pitfalls: Requires row context to work

name: USERELATIONSHIP
description_short: Activates an inactive relationship between two columns for the duration of the calculation.
notes: Can only be used inside CALCULATE or CALCULATETABLE
Only one relationship between two tables can be active at a time
pitfalls: The relationship must already exist in the model as inactive

name: DATEADD
description_short: Returns a table of dates shifted by the specified interval.

params.name: dates
params.description: A date column (must be from a marked date table)

params.name: numberOfIntervals
params.description: Number of intervals to shift (negative for past)

notes: Requires a marked date table in the model
Commonly used inside CALCULATE
pitfalls: Only works with contiguous date ranges
The date column must be from a date table

name: DATESYTD
description_short: Returns a table of dates from the beginning of the year up to the last date in the filter context.

params.name: yearEndDate
params.description: Optional year end date string (default: Dec 31)

notes: Used for Year-to-Date calculations
Second parameter allows fiscal year end dates
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: TOTALYTD
description_short: Evaluates an expression for year-to-date in the current context.
notes: Shorthand for CALCULATE(<expression>, DATESYTD(<dates>))
pitfalls: Less flexible than explicit CALCULATE + DATESYTD

name: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR
description_short: Returns a table of dates shifted back by one year from the current filter context.
notes: Equivalent to DATEADD(<dates>, -1, YEAR)
Used for year-over-year comparisons
pitfalls: Requires contiguous dates and a marked date table

name: ADDCOLUMNS
description_short: Adds calculated columns to a table expression.
notes: Creates row context for each expression
Useful with SUMMARIZE for adding measures to grouped results
pitfalls: Performance: avoid iterating over large fact tables with complex expressions

name: SELECTCOLUMNS
description_short: Returns a table with selected columns from a table expression.
notes: Only includes columns you explicitly specify
Can rename and transform columns
pitfalls: The resulting table loses data lineage (columns are disconnected from original)

name: SUMMARIZE
description_short: Returns a summary table grouped by the specified columns.
notes: Prefer SUMMARIZECOLUMNS for better performance
Can add extension columns but this is not recommended
pitfalls: Adding calculated columns directly in SUMMARIZE is deprecated; use ADDCOLUMNS(SUMMARIZE(...), ...) instead

name: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
description_short: Groups by specified columns and optionally adds measures. Highly optimized.
notes: Optimized by the engine; preferred over SUMMARIZE + ADDCOLUMNS
Cannot be used in measures; only in queries and calculated tables
pitfalls: Not usable inside measures
Automatically removes blank rows

name: TOPN
description_short: Returns the top N rows of a table sorted by an expression.
notes: May return more than N rows in case of ties
Useful with CALCULATE for top-N filtering
pitfalls: Ties can cause more rows than expected

name: UNION
description_short: Creates a union (concatenation) of two or more tables.
notes: Tables must have the same number of columns
Does not remove duplicates
pitfalls: Column data types must match by position

name: INTERSECT
description_short: Returns rows that appear in both tables.
notes: Returns only rows from table1 that also exist in table2
pitfalls: Column count and types must match

name: EXCEPT
description_short: Returns rows from table1 that do not appear in table2.
notes: Useful for finding missing or unmatched rows
pitfalls: Column count and types must match

name: GENERATE
description_short: Returns a cross-join of table1 with table2, evaluating table2 for each row of table1.

params.name: table2
params.description: Table expression evaluated per row of table1

notes: If table2 returns empty for a row, that row is excluded
Use GENERATEALL to keep rows with empty table2
pitfalls: Can produce very large result sets

name: ROW
description_short: Returns a single-row table with the specified columns and values.
notes: Useful for creating inline single-row tables

name: LOOKUPVALUE
description_short: Returns the value for a row that meets all specified search criteria.

params.name: result_column
params.description: The column containing the value to return

notes: Can have multiple search column/value pairs
Returns BLANK if no match and no alternate specified
pitfalls: Returns error if multiple matches found
Performance can be poor; prefer relationships when possible

name: SELECTEDVALUE
description_short: Returns the value when there is only one value in the filter context, otherwise returns alternate result.

params.name: alternateResult
params.description: Value if multiple or no values (default: BLANK())

notes: Equivalent to IF(HASONEVALUE(col), VALUES(col), alternate)
Commonly used for dynamic titles and conditional logic
pitfalls: Returns BLANK if column has multiple values in context and no alternate is specified

name: HASONEVALUE
description_short: Returns TRUE when there is only one distinct value in the specified column in the current filter context.
notes: Often used before VALUES() to safely extract a single value
pitfalls: Consider using SELECTEDVALUE which combines both checks

name: ISBLANK
description_short: Checks whether a value is BLANK.
notes: BLANK is DAX's equivalent of NULL
Consider COALESCE as a cleaner alternative to IF(ISBLANK(...), ...)
pitfalls: 0 and empty string are NOT blank in DAX

name: ISFILTERED
description_short: Returns TRUE when the specified column is being directly filtered.
notes: Returns TRUE for direct filters, FALSE for cross-filters
pitfalls: Does not detect cross-filters; use ISCROSSFILTERED for that

name: CONCATENATEX
description_short: Concatenates the result of an expression evaluated for each row, with a delimiter.
notes: Iterator function
Useful for creating comma-separated lists
pitfalls: Performance on large tables
No built-in DISTINCT; wrap table in VALUES or DISTINCT

name: FORMAT
description_short: Converts a value to text according to the specified format.
notes: Returns text, not a number
Supports custom date, number, and text formats
pitfalls: Result is text and cannot be used in calculations without conversion
Performance overhead in iterators

name: BLANK
description_short: Returns a blank value.
notes: DAX equivalent of NULL
Propagates through most calculations
pitfalls: BLANK + number = number (not blank)
BLANK in boolean context = FALSE

name: ERROR
description_short: Raises an error with the specified message.
notes: Useful for validating inputs in measures
Execution stops when encountered
pitfalls: Cannot be caught within DAX

name: CONTAINS
description_short: Returns TRUE if there exists at least one row matching all specified column-value pairs.
notes: Can check multiple column-value pairs simultaneously
pitfalls: Does not support wildcards or partial matching

name: EARLIER
description_short: Returns the value of a column in an outer row context.

params.name: column
params.description: Column to reference from outer context

params.name: number
params.description: Number of outer contexts to go back (default: 1)

notes: Legacy function for accessing outer row contexts
VAR is the modern preferred alternative
pitfalls: Difficult to read and maintain
Always prefer VAR for storing outer context values

name: CALENDAR
description_short: Returns a table with a single Date column containing a contiguous set of dates.
notes: Useful for creating date tables
Dates are inclusive on both ends
pitfalls: Only generates the Date column; add other columns with ADDCOLUMNS

name: DATE
description_short: Returns the specified date as a datetime value.
notes: Handles overflow: DATE(2023, 13, 1) = Jan 1, 2024

name: TODAY
description_short: Returns the current date.
notes: Returns date only (no time component)
Value changes each day
pitfalls: Not recommended for calculated columns as it recalculates on each refresh

name: YEAR
description_short: Returns the year of a date as a four-digit number.

name: MONTH
description_short: Returns the month of a date as a number from 1 to 12.

name: LEFT
description_short: Returns the specified number of characters from the start of a text string.

params.name: text
params.description: The text string containing the characters to extract

params.name: num_chars
params.description: The number of characters to extract

notes: If num_chars exceeds the length of text, returns the entire string
pitfalls: num_chars must be >= 0

name: RIGHT
description_short: Returns the specified number of characters from the end of a text string.

params.name: text
params.description: The text string containing the characters to extract

params.name: num_chars
params.description: The number of characters to extract

notes: If num_chars exceeds the length of text, returns the entire string
pitfalls: num_chars must be >= 0

name: MID
description_short: Returns a string of characters from the middle of a text string.

params.name: text
params.description: The text string containing the characters to extract

params.name: start_num
params.description: The position of the first character to extract (1-based)

params.name: num_chars
params.description: The number of characters to extract

notes: start_num is 1-based
pitfalls: If start_num is greater than the length of text, returns empty string

name: LEN
description_short: Returns the number of characters in a text string.
notes: Counts all characters including spaces
pitfalls: BLANK returns 0

name: UPPER
description_short: Converts a text string to all uppercase.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to convert to uppercase

notes: Non-alphabetic characters are unchanged

name: LOWER
description_short: Converts a text string to all lowercase.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to convert to lowercase

notes: Non-alphabetic characters are unchanged

name: TRIM
description_short: Removes all leading and trailing spaces from a text string.

params.name: text
params.description: The text from which to remove spaces

notes: Also reduces internal multiple spaces to single spaces
pitfalls: Does not remove non-breaking spaces; use SUBSTITUTE to handle those

name: SUBSTITUTE
description_short: Replaces occurrences of existing text with new text in a string.

params.name: text
params.description: The text in which to substitute

params.name: instance_num
params.description: Which occurrence to replace (optional; if omitted, all occurrences are replaced)

notes: Case-sensitive matching
If instance_num is omitted, all occurrences are replaced
pitfalls: Case-sensitive; 'A' and 'a' are treated differently

name: FIND
description_short: Returns the starting position of one text string within another (case-sensitive).

params.name: start_num
params.description: Position to start searching from (optional, default 1)

params.name: notFoundValue
params.description: Value to return if text is not found (optional)

notes: Case-sensitive
1-based position
pitfalls: Returns an error if text is not found and notFoundValue is not specified

name: SEARCH
description_short: Returns the starting position of one text string within another (case-insensitive).

params.name: start_num
params.description: Position to start searching from (optional, default 1)

params.name: notFoundValue
params.description: Value to return if text is not found (optional)

notes: Case-insensitive
Supports wildcards: ? for single character, * for any sequence
pitfalls: Returns an error if text is not found and notFoundValue is not specified

name: CONCATENATE
description_short: Joins two text strings into one.
notes: Only accepts two arguments; use & operator or CONCATENATEX for multiple strings
pitfalls: For joining more than two strings, use the & operator or CONCATENATEX

name: REPT
description_short: Repeats text a given number of times.

params.name: number_times
params.description: The number of times to repeat the text

notes: If number_times is 0, returns empty string
pitfalls: Result is limited to 32767 characters

name: FIXED
description_short: Rounds a number to the specified number of decimals and returns the result as text.

params.name: number
params.description: The number to round and convert

params.name: no_commas
params.description: If TRUE, do not include commas (optional, default FALSE)

notes: Returns text, not a number
pitfalls: Result is text and cannot be used directly in arithmetic

name: EXACT
description_short: Compares two text strings and returns TRUE if they are exactly the same (case-sensitive).
notes: Case-sensitive comparison
Numbers are compared as text
pitfalls: Unlike =, EXACT is case-sensitive

name: SQRT
description_short: Returns the square root of a number.

params.name: number
params.description: The number to get the square root of

notes: Number must be non-negative
pitfalls: Returns error for negative numbers

name: POWER
description_short: Returns the result of a number raised to a power.
notes: Equivalent to the ^ operator
pitfalls: POWER(0, 0) returns 1

name: LOG
description_short: Returns the logarithm of a number to the specified base.

params.name: number
params.description: The positive number for which to calculate the logarithm

params.name: base
params.description: The base of the logarithm (optional, default 10)

notes: Default base is 10 if not specified
pitfalls: Number must be positive

name: LOG10
description_short: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.

params.name: number
params.description: The positive number for which to calculate the base-10 logarithm

notes: Equivalent to LOG(number, 10)
pitfalls: Number must be positive

name: MOD
description_short: Returns the remainder after a number is divided by a divisor.
notes: Result has the same sign as the divisor
pitfalls: Divisor cannot be 0

name: CEILING
description_short: Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance.

params.name: significance
params.description: The multiple to which to round

notes: Rounds away from zero for positive numbers
pitfalls: Number and significance must have the same sign

name: FLOOR
description_short: Rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance.

params.name: significance
params.description: The multiple to which to round

notes: Rounds toward zero for positive numbers
pitfalls: Number and significance must have the same sign

name: EVEN
description_short: Returns a number rounded up to the nearest even integer.
notes: Rounds away from zero
pitfalls: Negative numbers round away from zero: EVEN(-3) = -4

name: ODD
description_short: Returns a number rounded up to the nearest odd integer.
notes: Rounds away from zero
pitfalls: Negative numbers round away from zero: ODD(-2) = -3

name: RAND
description_short: Returns a random number greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.
notes: Returns a new random number each time the model is recalculated
pitfalls: Not suitable for cryptographic purposes
Recalculates on every refresh

name: SIGN
description_short: Returns the sign of a number: 1 for positive, 0 for zero, -1 for negative.

params.name: number
params.description: The number to determine the sign of

notes: Returns -1, 0, or 1

name: TRUNC
description_short: Truncates a number to an integer by removing the fractional part, or to specified decimal places.

params.name: num_digits
params.description: Number of decimal places to keep (optional, default 0)

notes: Unlike ROUND, TRUNC simply removes digits without rounding
pitfalls: TRUNC(-3.7) returns -3, not -4 (unlike INT which returns -4)

name: PI
description_short: Returns the value of pi, 3.14159265358979.
notes: Returns the mathematical constant pi with 15-digit precision

name: NOW
description_short: Returns the current date and time.
notes: Includes both date and time components
Value changes each time the model is refreshed
pitfalls: Not recommended for calculated columns as it recalculates on each refresh

name: DATEDIFF
description_short: Returns the difference between two dates in the specified interval.

params.name: interval
params.description: The unit of interval: SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER, or YEAR

notes: Returns a negative value if start_date is after end_date
pitfalls: MONTH and YEAR intervals use calendar boundaries, not fixed durations

name: EOMONTH
description_short: Returns the date of the last day of the month, N months before or after the start date.

params.name: months
params.description: Number of months before (negative) or after (positive) start_date

notes: Useful for calculating month-end dates
months = 0 returns the end of the current month
pitfalls: Returns the last day of the month, not the same day in another month

name: DAY
description_short: Returns the day of the month as a number from 1 to 31.

name: HOUR
description_short: Returns the hour as a number from 0 to 23.
notes: Returns 0-23 (24-hour format)

name: MINUTE
description_short: Returns the minute as a number from 0 to 59.

name: SECOND
description_short: Returns the second as a number from 0 to 59.

name: WEEKDAY
description_short: Returns a number identifying the day of the week of a date.

params.name: return_type
params.description: Determines the return value mapping (optional, default 1: Sunday=1 to Saturday=7)

notes: return_type 1: Sunday=1..Saturday=7
return_type 2: Monday=1..Sunday=7
pitfalls: Different return_type values produce different numbering schemes

name: WEEKNUM
description_short: Returns the week number of the year for a given date.

params.name: return_type
params.description: Determines which day is the start of the week (optional, default 1: Sunday)

notes: return_type 1: week begins on Sunday
return_type 2: week begins on Monday
pitfalls: Week numbering may differ from ISO week numbers

name: QUARTER
description_short: Returns the quarter of the year as a number from 1 to 4.
notes: Q1=Jan-Mar, Q2=Apr-Jun, Q3=Jul-Sep, Q4=Oct-Dec

name: STARTOFYEAR
description_short: Returns the first date of the year in the current filter context.

params.name: year_end_date
params.description: Optional year end date for fiscal year (e.g., "06-30")

notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: STARTOFMONTH
description_short: Returns the first date of the month in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: STARTOFQUARTER
description_short: Returns the first date of the quarter in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: ENDOFYEAR
description_short: Returns the last date of the year in the current filter context.

params.name: year_end_date
params.description: Optional year end date for fiscal year (e.g., "06-30")

notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: ENDOFMONTH
description_short: Returns the last date of the month in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: ENDOFQUARTER
description_short: Returns the last date of the quarter in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table that can be used as a scalar
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: PARALLELPERIOD
description_short: Returns a table of dates representing a period parallel to the current dates, shifted by the specified intervals.

params.name: number_of_intervals
params.description: Number of intervals to shift (negative for past)

notes: Returns a full period (e.g., full month or year) unlike DATEADD which preserves the original date range
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table
Returns full periods, not partial ones

name: PREVIOUSYEAR
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the previous year from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the previous year
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: PREVIOUSMONTH
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the previous month from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the previous month
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: PREVIOUSQUARTER
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the previous quarter from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the previous quarter
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: PREVIOUSDAY
description_short: Returns a table containing the date of the previous day from the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-date table
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: NEXTYEAR
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the next year from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the next year
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: NEXTMONTH
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the next month from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the next month
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: NEXTQUARTER
description_short: Returns a table of all dates in the next quarter from the current filter context.
notes: Returns all dates in the next quarter
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: NEXTDAY
description_short: Returns a table containing the date of the next day from the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-date table
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: DATESBETWEEN
description_short: Returns a table of dates between the specified start and end dates.
notes: Both start and end dates are inclusive
Use BLANK() for open-ended ranges
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: DATESINPERIOD
description_short: Returns a table of dates starting from the start date for the specified number of intervals.

params.name: number_of_intervals
params.description: Number of intervals (negative for going backward)

notes: Negative intervals go backward from the start date
Useful for rolling period calculations
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: TOTALMTD
description_short: Evaluates an expression for the month-to-date in the current context.
notes: Shorthand for CALCULATE(<expression>, DATESMTD(<dates>))
pitfalls: Less flexible than explicit CALCULATE + DATESMTD

name: TOTALQTD
description_short: Evaluates an expression for the quarter-to-date in the current context.
notes: Shorthand for CALCULATE(<expression>, DATESQTD(<dates>))
pitfalls: Less flexible than explicit CALCULATE + DATESQTD

name: OPENINGBALANCEYEAR
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date before the start of the year in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the opening of the year (last day of previous year)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: OPENINGBALANCEMONTH
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date before the start of the month in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the opening of the month (last day of previous month)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: OPENINGBALANCEQUARTER
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date before the start of the quarter in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the opening of the quarter (last day of previous quarter)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: CLOSINGBALANCEYEAR
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date of the year in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the closing of the year (last day of the year)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date of the month in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the closing of the month (last day of the month)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: CLOSINGBALANCEQUARTER
description_short: Evaluates an expression at the last date of the quarter in the current context.
notes: Returns the value at the closing of the quarter (last day of the quarter)
pitfalls: Requires a marked date table

name: FIRSTDATE
description_short: Returns the first date in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table
Respects the current filter context
pitfalls: Returns a table, not a scalar; use in CALCULATE or wrap with scalar extraction

name: LASTDATE
description_short: Returns the last date in the current filter context.
notes: Returns a single-row, single-column table
Respects the current filter context
pitfalls: Returns a table, not a scalar; use in CALCULATE or wrap with scalar extraction

name: MEDIAN
description_short: Returns the median value of a column.
notes: For an even number of values, returns the average of the two middle values
pitfalls: Ignores blank values

name: MEDIANX
description_short: Returns the median of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function; evaluates expression row by row
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded

name: STDEV.S
description_short: Returns the sample standard deviation of a column.
notes: Uses the sample formula (n-1 denominator)
pitfalls: Ignores blank values
Requires at least two values

name: STDEV.P
description_short: Returns the population standard deviation of a column.
notes: Uses the population formula (n denominator)
pitfalls: Ignores blank values

name: STDEVX.S
description_short: Returns the sample standard deviation of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function using sample formula (n-1 denominator)
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded

name: STDEVX.P
description_short: Returns the population standard deviation of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function using population formula (n denominator)
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded

name: VAR.S
description_short: Returns the sample variance of a column.
notes: Uses the sample formula (n-1 denominator)
This is the statistical variance function, not the VAR variable keyword
pitfalls: Ignores blank values
Requires at least two values

name: VAR.P
description_short: Returns the population variance of a column.
notes: Uses the population formula (n denominator)
pitfalls: Ignores blank values

name: VARX.S
description_short: Returns the sample variance of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function using sample formula (n-1 denominator)
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded

name: VARX.P
description_short: Returns the population variance of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function using population formula (n denominator)
pitfalls: Blank expression results are excluded

name: PERCENTILE.INC
description_short: Returns the k-th percentile of values in a column (inclusive).
notes: k=0.5 returns the median
Inclusive: k can be 0 or 1
pitfalls: k must be between 0 and 1 inclusive

name: PERCENTILE.EXC
description_short: Returns the k-th percentile of values in a column (exclusive).
notes: Exclusive: k must be strictly between 0 and 1
pitfalls: k must be strictly between 0 and 1 (not equal to 0 or 1)

name: PERCENTILEX.INC
description_short: Returns the k-th percentile of an expression evaluated for each row in a table (inclusive).

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function
Inclusive: k can be 0 or 1
pitfalls: k must be between 0 and 1 inclusive

name: PERCENTILEX.EXC
description_short: Returns the k-th percentile of an expression evaluated for each row in a table (exclusive).

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function
Exclusive: k must be strictly between 0 and 1
pitfalls: k must be strictly between 0 and 1 (not equal to 0 or 1)

name: ISNUMBER
description_short: Returns TRUE if the value is a number.
notes: Useful for data validation
pitfalls: BLANK is not considered a number

name: ISTEXT
description_short: Returns TRUE if the value is text.
notes: Useful for data validation
pitfalls: BLANK is not considered text

name: ISERROR
description_short: Returns TRUE if the value is an error.
notes: Checks for any error type
Often used with IF for error handling
pitfalls: Consider using IFERROR for simpler error handling

name: ISLOGICAL
description_short: Returns TRUE if the value is a logical (TRUE/FALSE) value.
notes: Tests specifically for TRUE or FALSE values
pitfalls: BLANK is not considered a logical value

name: ISINSCOPE
description_short: Returns TRUE when the specified column is the level in a hierarchy of levels.

params.name: column
params.description: Column to check if it is in scope

notes: Useful for conditional formatting and dynamic measures in matrix visuals
Returns TRUE when column is being grouped by in the current context
pitfalls: Different from ISFILTERED; ISINSCOPE checks if the column is used for grouping

name: ISNONTEXT
description_short: Returns TRUE if the value is not text.
notes: BLANK returns TRUE (blank is not text)
pitfalls: Opposite of ISTEXT but also returns TRUE for BLANK

name: ISEVEN
description_short: Returns TRUE if the number is even.
notes: Number is truncated to integer before testing
pitfalls: Non-numeric values cause an error

name: ISODD
description_short: Returns TRUE if the number is odd.
notes: Number is truncated to integer before testing
pitfalls: Non-numeric values cause an error

name: USERPRINCIPALNAME
description_short: Returns the user principal name (UPN) of the current user.
notes: Commonly used for row-level security (RLS)
Returns the UPN from Azure AD / Microsoft Entra ID
pitfalls: Returns the service account in scheduled refresh scenarios
Only works in Power BI Service, not in Desktop during development

name: USERNAME
description_short: Returns the domain and username of the current user.
notes: Returns in domain\username format
Used for row-level security
pitfalls: Prefer USERPRINCIPALNAME for cloud-based RLS

name: IFERROR
description_short: Returns value_if_error if the first argument evaluates to an error, otherwise returns the first argument.

params.name: value_if_error
params.description: The value to return if the first argument is an error

notes: Cleaner alternative to IF(ISERROR(...), ..., ...)
pitfalls: Both arguments must return compatible data types

name: CROSSJOIN
description_short: Returns the Cartesian product of two or more tables.
notes: Result has all columns from all tables
Row count is the product of all table row counts
pitfalls: Can produce very large result sets
Column names must not conflict across tables

name: NATURALINNERJOIN
description_short: Performs an inner join of two tables using common columns.
notes: Joins on columns with the same name and data lineage
Only returns rows that match in both tables
pitfalls: Requires common columns with the same lineage

name: NATURALLEFTOUTERJOIN
description_short: Performs a left outer join of two tables using common columns.
notes: Returns all rows from the left table
Unmatched rows from the left table have BLANK values for right table columns
pitfalls: Requires common columns with the same lineage

name: DISTINCT
description_short: Returns a one-column table of distinct values from a column, or a table with distinct row combinations.
notes: Unlike VALUES, DISTINCT does not include the blank row for invalid relationships
pitfalls: Does not include the blank row that VALUES would include

name: GENERATESERIES
description_short: Returns a single-column table containing a sequence of values.

params.name: end
params.description: The ending value (inclusive if reached by step)

notes: Column is named [Value]
End value is included if exactly reached by step increments
pitfalls: Step must be positive if start < end, or negative if start > end

name: DATATABLE
description_short: Creates an inline table with specified columns, data types, and data.

params.name: type1
params.description: Data type (INTEGER, DOUBLE, STRING, BOOLEAN, DATETIME)

params.name: data
params.description: The data rows enclosed in double curly braces

notes: Data is provided in row sets within double curly braces {{...}}
Useful for creating small reference tables inline
pitfalls: Only supports basic data types
Not suitable for large tables

name: GROUPBY
description_short: Groups a table by specified columns and adds summary columns using CURRENTGROUP().

params.name: expression
params.description: Expression using CURRENTGROUP() to compute aggregation

notes: Extension columns must use CURRENTGROUP() with an X-aggregation function
More flexible than SUMMARIZE for complex grouping
pitfalls: CURRENTGROUP() can only be used inside GROUPBY extension columns

name: ALLSELECTED
description_short: Removes context filters from columns and rows in the current query while retaining all other filters from slicers and external filters.
notes: Commonly used for percentage-of-visible-total calculations
Respects slicer and page-level filter selections
pitfalls: Complex interaction with nested CALCULATE contexts
May produce unexpected results in visual calculations

name: ALLNOBLANKROW
description_short: Returns all rows in a table or all values in a column, ignoring filters, but excluding the blank row.
notes: Like ALL but excludes the blank row that appears for invalid relationships
pitfalls: Only differs from ALL when there are blank rows from broken relationships

name: COUNTBLANK
description_short: Counts the number of blank values in a column.

params.name: column
params.description: The column to count blank values in

notes: Counts BLANK values and empty strings
Complement of COUNTA
pitfalls: Empty strings are counted as blank

name: COUNTA
description_short: Counts the number of non-blank values in a column.

params.name: column
params.description: The column to count non-blank values in

notes: Counts any non-blank value regardless of data type
Works with text, numbers, dates, and logical values
pitfalls: Unlike COUNT, COUNTA works with all data types, not just numbers

name: COUNTAX
description_short: Counts the number of non-blank results of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function, counts non-blank expression results
pitfalls: Blank expression results are not counted

name: PRODUCTX
description_short: Returns the product of an expression evaluated for each row in a table.

params.name: table
params.description: The table over which to iterate

notes: Iterator function that multiplies results together
Useful for compound growth calculations
pitfalls: A single zero in the results will make the entire product zero

name: FIRSTNONBLANK
description_short: Returns the first value in a column where the expression is not blank.

params.name: expression
params.description: Expression evaluated for each row; returns the first column value where this is not blank

notes: Scans column values in ascending order
Returns a single-row table
pitfalls: Column values are evaluated in ascending order

name: LASTNONBLANK
description_short: Returns the last value in a column where the expression is not blank.

params.name: expression
params.description: Expression evaluated for each row; returns the last column value where this is not blank

notes: Scans column values in descending order
Returns a single-row table
pitfalls: Column values are evaluated in descending order

name: COUNTX
description_short: Counts non-blank results when evaluating an expression for each row of a table.
notes: Iterator function — evaluates expression per row
Only counts non-blank results
pitfalls: Empty strings are counted (not blank)

name: AVERAGEA
description_short: Returns the average of values in a column, treating TRUE as 1, FALSE as 0, and text as 0.
notes: Treats TRUE as 1, FALSE as 0, text as 0
Ignores blanks
pitfalls: Different from AVERAGE which ignores non-numeric

name: MAXA
description_short: Returns the largest value in a column, including logical and text values.
notes: TRUE = 1, FALSE = 0, text = 0
Blanks are ignored
pitfalls: May give unexpected results with mixed types

name: MINA
description_short: Returns the smallest value in a column, including logical and text values.
notes: TRUE = 1, FALSE = 0, text = 0
Blanks are ignored
pitfalls: May give unexpected results with mixed types

name: PRODUCT
description_short: Returns the product of all numbers in a column.
notes: Multiplies all values together
Ignores blanks and non-numeric
pitfalls: A single zero makes the entire result zero

name: DISTINCTCOUNTNOBLANK
description_short: Counts the number of distinct values in a column, excluding blanks.
notes: Unlike DISTINCTCOUNT, does not count BLANK
pitfalls: Slightly faster than DISTINCTCOUNT when blanks don't matter

name: APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT
description_short: Returns an approximate count of distinct values using HyperLogLog.
notes: Uses HyperLogLog algorithm for performance
Only available in DirectQuery mode
pitfalls: Result is approximate, not exact
Only works with DirectQuery

name: CALENDARAUTO
description_short: Returns a contiguous date table based on dates found in the model.

params.name: fiscal_year_end_month
params.description: Month number (1-12) for fiscal year end. Default is 12.

notes: Scans all date columns in the model to determine range
Returns single column named Date
pitfalls: May include unexpected date ranges from columns you didn't intend

name: EDATE
description_short: Returns a date that is the specified number of months before or after a date.

params.name: months
params.description: Number of months to add (negative to subtract)

notes: Handles month-end dates correctly
pitfalls: If start date is end of month, result is also end of month

name: DATEVALUE
description_short: Converts a date in text format to a date value.
notes: Recognizes common date formats
pitfalls: Date format depends on locale settings

name: TIME
description_short: Converts hours, minutes, and seconds to a time value.
notes: Returns a fractional day value
pitfalls: Values greater than 23/59/59 roll over

name: TIMEVALUE
description_short: Converts a time in text format to a time value.
notes: Returns a decimal number for the time
pitfalls: Format depends on locale

name: UTCNOW
description_short: Returns the current UTC date and time.
notes: Returns UTC, not local time
pitfalls: Value is fixed when query starts, not continuously updating

name: UTCTODAY
description_short: Returns the current UTC date.
notes: Returns date only (no time component)
pitfalls: Returns UTC date, which may differ from local date

name: DATESMTD
description_short: Returns a table of dates from the beginning of the month to the last date in the specified column.
notes: Month-to-date equivalent of DATESYTD
pitfalls: Requires a proper date table

name: DATESQTD
description_short: Returns a table of dates from the beginning of the quarter to the last date in the specified column.
notes: Quarter-to-date equivalent of DATESYTD
pitfalls: Requires a proper date table

name: FIRSTNONBLANKVALUE
description_short: Returns the first non-blank value of an expression evaluated over a column sorted in ascending order.
notes: Evaluates expression in the filter context of each row
pitfalls: Different from FIRSTNONBLANK which returns a table

name: LASTNONBLANKVALUE
description_short: Returns the last non-blank value of an expression evaluated over a column sorted in ascending order.
notes: Useful for semi-additive measures like inventory snapshots
pitfalls: Different from LASTNONBLANK which returns a table

name: ALLCROSSFILTERED
description_short: Clears all filters applied to a table, including cross-filters from related tables.
notes: More aggressive than ALL — removes cross-filters too
pitfalls: Can produce unexpected results in complex models

name: EARLIEST
description_short: Returns the value of the specified column in an outer evaluation pass.

params.name: column
params.description: Column to retrieve outer value from

notes: Deprecated — use VAR instead
References the outermost row context
pitfalls: Confusing semantics, VAR is always preferred

name: INDEX
description_short: Returns a row at an absolute position within a partition, sorted by the specified order.
notes: Window function — use with ORDERBY and PARTITIONBY
Returns a single-row table
pitfalls: Requires careful use of ORDERBY

name: OFFSET
description_short: Returns a row that is a given number of rows before or after the current row within a partition.

params.name: delta
params.description: Number of rows to offset (negative for before)

notes: Window function for relative row access
Commonly used for previous/next row values
pitfalls: Returns blank if offset goes beyond partition edges

name: WINDOW
description_short: Returns multiple rows within a window defined by from/to positions relative to current row.
notes: Most flexible window function
Supports both absolute and relative positions
pitfalls: Complex syntax — consider INDEX or OFFSET for simpler cases

name: RANK
description_short: Returns the rank of a row within a partition.
notes: Window function that returns a rank
Ties get the same rank (with gaps)
pitfalls: Different from RANKX which uses a different approach

name: ROWNUMBER
description_short: Returns the unique row number within a partition.
notes: Always returns unique numbers (no ties)
pitfalls: Tie-breaking is non-deterministic without sufficient ORDERBY columns

name: ORDERBY
description_short: Defines the sort order for window functions (INDEX, OFFSET, WINDOW, RANK, ROWNUMBER).
notes: Used as argument to window functions, not standalone
Can specify multiple columns
pitfalls: Must be used inside a window function call

name: PARTITIONBY
description_short: Defines the partition for window functions (INDEX, OFFSET, WINDOW, RANK, ROWNUMBER).
notes: Used as argument to window functions
Creates subgroups within which the window function operates
pitfalls: Must be used inside a window function call

name: MATCHBY
description_short: Defines the columns used to identify the current row in window functions.
notes: Used when the default row identification is ambiguous
Typically needed with SUMMARIZE or calculated tables
pitfalls: Only needed in advanced scenarios

name: IF.EAGER
description_short: Same as IF but evaluates both branches regardless of the condition. Can improve performance in some cases.
notes: Evaluates both branches eagerly (no short-circuit)
Can be faster when both branches share similar calculations
pitfalls: Both branches are always evaluated, even if one isn't used

name: CONTAINSROW
description_short: Returns TRUE if at least one row in the table has the specified values.

params.name: value1
params.description: Value to match in the first column

notes: Simpler syntax than CONTAINS for value checking
Checks column values in order
pitfalls: Values must match column order in the table

name: CONTAINSSTRING
description_short: Returns TRUE if one string contains another (case-insensitive).
notes: Case-insensitive search
Supports wildcards (* and ?)
pitfalls: Use CONTAINSSTRINGEXACT for case-sensitive search

name: CONTAINSSTRINGEXACT
description_short: Returns TRUE if one string contains another (case-sensitive).
notes: Case-sensitive version of CONTAINSSTRING
pitfalls: Does not support wildcards

name: HASONEFILTER
description_short: Returns TRUE when there is exactly one filter on the specified column.
notes: Checks for exactly one direct filter value
Useful for conditional formatting logic
pitfalls: Different from HASONEVALUE which checks for one visible value

name: ISEMPTY
description_short: Returns TRUE if a table is empty (contains no rows).
notes: Efficient way to check for empty tables
Stops scanning at first row
pitfalls: Evaluates the table expression

name: ISCROSSFILTERED
description_short: Returns TRUE when the specified column is being cross-filtered.
notes: Detects both direct and cross-filters
Returns TRUE if any filter exists on the column's table
pitfalls: More inclusive than ISFILTERED

name: ISSUBTOTAL
description_short: Returns TRUE when the current row is a subtotal row created by SUMMARIZECOLUMNS with ROLLUP.
notes: Only meaningful with SUMMARIZECOLUMNS + ROLLUP
Used to conditionally format subtotal rows
pitfalls: Only works in specific SUMMARIZECOLUMNS context

name: NAMEOF
description_short: Returns the name of a column as a text string.
notes: Returns the column name without the table prefix
pitfalls: Returns the column name, not the table name

name: USERCULTURE
description_short: Returns the locale of the current user as a text string.
notes: Returns locale string like "en-US"
Useful for locale-aware formatting
pitfalls: May not be available in all environments

name: USEROBJECTID
description_short: Returns the Object ID of the current user from Azure AD.
notes: Returns the Azure AD object ID
Used for row-level security
pitfalls: Only works in Power BI Service, not Desktop

name: COMBINEVALUES
description_short: Joins two or more text strings into one, using the specified delimiter.
notes: Optimized for DirectQuery — generates efficient SQL
Preferred over CONCATENATE for composite keys
pitfalls: All values are converted to text

name: REPLACE
description_short: Replaces part of a text string with a different text string by position.
notes: Position-based replacement (not pattern-based)
Use SUBSTITUTE for find-and-replace by value
pitfalls: 1-based indexing

name: VALUE
description_short: Converts a text string that represents a number to a number.
notes: Equivalent to using + 0 on a text value
pitfalls: Returns error if text cannot be converted

name: UNICHAR
description_short: Returns the Unicode character referenced by the given number.
notes: Useful for inserting special characters
pitfalls: Invalid code points return an error

name: UNICODE
description_short: Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of a text string.
notes: Returns code point of first character only
pitfalls: Returns error for empty string

name: GENERATEALL
description_short: Like GENERATE, but includes rows where the second table is empty (with blanks).

params.name: table2
params.description: Table expression evaluated for each row of table1

notes: Keeps all rows from table1, even if table2 is empty
Similar to a LEFT OUTER JOIN
pitfalls: Returns blank values for unmatched rows

name: CURRENTGROUP
description_short: Returns the rows in the current group of a GROUPBY expression.
notes: Only valid inside GROUPBY expressions
Used with aggregation X functions
pitfalls: Cannot be used outside GROUPBY

name: FILTERS
description_short: Returns the values that are directly filtered on the specified column.
notes: Returns only direct filter values, not cross-filters
Useful for debugging filter context
pitfalls: Different from VALUES which respects all filters

name: ADDMISSINGITEMS
description_short: Adds rows with missing items to a table returned by SUMMARIZECOLUMNS.

params.name: showAll_column
params.description: Column whose missing items to add

notes: Used with SUMMARIZECOLUMNS to show blank rows
pitfalls: Complex function, typically auto-generated by tools

name: DETAILROWS
description_short: Returns the detail rows expression defined for a measure.

params.name: measure
params.description: A measure with detail rows defined

notes: Returns the detail rows expression from the measure metadata
Used in drill-through scenarios
pitfalls: Only works if the measure has a detail rows expression defined

name: IGNORE
description_short: Modifies SUMMARIZECOLUMNS by omitting specific expressions from the blank-row check.

params.name: expression
params.description: Expression to ignore during blank-row removal

notes: Used only inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
Prevents the expression from causing blank rows to be removed
pitfalls: Only meaningful within SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

name: SUBSTITUTEWITHINDEX
description_short: Replaces columns in a table with a compact index, typically for performance optimization.
notes: Performance optimization function
Used internally by tools
pitfalls: Rarely used directly in user measures

name: CROSSFILTER
description_short: Specifies the cross-filtering direction for a relationship in a CALCULATE expression.

params.name: column1
params.description: Column from one side of relationship

params.name: column2
params.description: Column from other side of relationship

params.name: direction
params.description: NONE, ONEWAY, BOTH, or ONEWAY_RIGHTFILTERSLEFT, ONEWAY_LEFTFILTERSRIGHT

notes: Used as a filter argument in CALCULATE
Overrides the model relationship direction
pitfalls: Must reference columns that form an existing relationship

name: LN
description_short: Returns the natural logarithm of a number.
notes: Base-e logarithm
pitfalls: Returns error for non-positive numbers

name: EXP
description_short: Returns e raised to the power of a number.
notes: Inverse of LN
pitfalls: Large exponents can overflow

name: ROUNDDOWN
description_short: Rounds a number down, toward zero.
notes: Always rounds toward zero
Use negative num_digits to round to tens, hundreds, etc.
pitfalls: Rounds toward zero, not toward negative infinity

name: ROUNDUP
description_short: Rounds a number up, away from zero.
notes: Always rounds away from zero
pitfalls: Rounds away from zero, not toward positive infinity

name: MROUND
description_short: Rounds a number to the nearest multiple of a specified value.
notes: Rounds to nearest multiple
pitfalls: Number and multiple must have the same sign

name: RANDBETWEEN
description_short: Returns a random integer between two specified values.
notes: Returns a different value each time the formula is recalculated
pitfalls: Not suitable for cryptographic purposes

name: CONVERT
description_short: Converts an expression to the specified data type.

params.name: dataType
params.description: Target type: INTEGER, DOUBLE, STRING, BOOLEAN, CURRENCY, DATETIME

notes: Explicit type conversion function
pitfalls: Returns error if conversion is not possible

name: CURRENCY
description_short: Converts a value to currency data type.
notes: Fixed-point decimal with 4 decimal places
pitfalls: Precision limited to 4 decimal places

name: PATH
description_short: Returns a delimited text string with the identifiers of all parents of the current row.
notes: Returns pipe-delimited path like '1|2|3'
Used for parent-child hierarchies
pitfalls: Circular references cause errors

name: PATHCONTAINS
description_short: Returns TRUE if the specified item exists in the specified path.
notes: Searches within a pipe-delimited path string
pitfalls: Item is matched as text

name: PATHITEM
description_short: Returns the item at the specified position from a path string.
notes: 1-based position from the root
pitfalls: Returns BLANK if position exceeds path length

name: PATHITEMREVERSE
description_short: Returns the item at the specified position from a path string, counting from the end.
notes: Position 1 is the last (current) item
pitfalls: Returns BLANK if position exceeds path length

name: PATHLENGTH
description_short: Returns the number of items in a path string (the depth of the node).
notes: Counts pipe-delimited items
pitfalls: Empty string returns 0

name: EVALUATEANDLOG
description_short: Returns the value of the expression and logs it for debugging in DAX query view.
notes: Debugging tool — outputs to Performance Analyzer
Does not affect the result
pitfalls: Only works in certain environments

name: TOCSV
description_short: Returns a table as a CSV-formatted text string.
notes: Useful for debugging table expressions
pitfalls: Large tables may be truncated

name: TOJSON
description_short: Returns a table as a JSON-formatted text string.
notes: Useful for debugging table expressions
pitfalls: Large tables may be truncated

name: EXTERNALMEASURE
description_short: References a measure defined externally, such as in a semantic model.
notes: Used for composite models
pitfalls: Requires external measure to be accessible

name: NONVISUAL
description_short: Marks a filter argument in SUMMARIZECOLUMNS as non-visual, preventing it from affecting grouping.
notes: Only used inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
pitfalls: Has no effect outside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

name: SAMPLE
description_short: Returns a sample of N rows from the specified table.
notes: Returns evenly distributed sample rows
If N >= table rows, returns all rows
pitfalls: Not random — returns evenly spaced rows

name: SELECTEDMEASURE
description_short: References the measure currently in context, used in calculation group expressions.
notes: Only valid inside calculation group items
Acts as a placeholder for whatever measure is being evaluated
pitfalls: Returns error outside calculation groups

name: SELECTEDMEASUREFORMATSTRING
description_short: Returns the format string of the measure currently in context.
notes: Used in calculation group format string expressions
pitfalls: Only valid in calculation groups

name: SELECTEDMEASURENAME
description_short: Returns the name of the measure currently in context.
notes: Used in calculation groups for conditional logic
pitfalls: Only valid in calculation groups

name: ISSELECTEDMEASURE
description_short: Returns TRUE if the measure in context matches one of the specified measures.
notes: Used in calculation groups for conditional formatting
pitfalls: Only valid in calculation groups

name: SIN
description_short: Returns the sine of an angle in radians.
notes: Input must be in radians
pitfalls: Use RADIANS() to convert degrees

name: COS
description_short: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.
notes: Input must be in radians
pitfalls: Use RADIANS() to convert degrees

name: TAN
description_short: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.
notes: Input must be in radians
pitfalls: Undefined at PI/2 + n*PI

name: ASIN
description_short: Returns the arcsine (inverse sine) of a number, in radians.
notes: Result in range [-PI/2, PI/2]
pitfalls: Error if input outside [-1, 1]

name: ACOS
description_short: Returns the arccosine (inverse cosine) of a number, in radians.
notes: Result in range [0, PI]
pitfalls: Error if input outside [-1, 1]

name: ATAN
description_short: Returns the arctangent (inverse tangent) of a number, in radians.
notes: Result in range (-PI/2, PI/2)

name: SINH
description_short: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number.
pitfalls: Large values can overflow

name: COSH
description_short: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number.
pitfalls: Large values can overflow

name: TANH
description_short: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number.
notes: Result always between -1 and 1

name: ASINH
description_short: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number.

name: ACOSH
description_short: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number.
pitfalls: Error if input < 1

name: ATANH
description_short: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number.
pitfalls: Error if input outside (-1, 1)

name: COT
description_short: Returns the cotangent of an angle in radians.
notes: Reciprocal of tangent
pitfalls: Undefined at multiples of PI

name: ACOT
description_short: Returns the inverse cotangent (arccotangent) of a number, in radians.
notes: Result in range (0, PI)

name: COTH
description_short: Returns the hyperbolic cotangent of a number.
pitfalls: Undefined at 0

name: ACOTH
description_short: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cotangent of a number.
pitfalls: Error if |input| <= 1

name: DEGREES
description_short: Converts radians to degrees.

name: RADIANS
description_short: Converts degrees to radians.

name: FACT
description_short: Returns the factorial of a number.
notes: FACT(0) = 1
pitfalls: Large numbers overflow quickly

name: GCD
description_short: Returns the greatest common divisor of two or more integers.
notes: Values are truncated to integers

name: LCM
description_short: Returns the least common multiple of two or more integers.
notes: Values are truncated to integers

name: QUOTIENT
description_short: Returns the integer portion of a division.
notes: Discards the remainder
pitfalls: Division by zero returns error

name: SQRTPI
description_short: Returns the square root of (number * PI).

params.name: number
params.description: Number to multiply by PI before taking square root

pitfalls: Error if number * PI is negative

name: ISO.CEILING
description_short: Rounds a number up to the nearest integer or multiple of significance, using ISO rounding rules.
notes: Uses ISO semantics for negative numbers
pitfalls: Different from CEILING for negative numbers

name: BITAND
description_short: Returns a bitwise AND of two numbers.
notes: Operates on 48-bit integers
pitfalls: Numbers are truncated to integers

name: BITOR
description_short: Returns a bitwise OR of two numbers.
notes: Operates on 48-bit integers
pitfalls: Numbers are truncated to integers

name: BITXOR
description_short: Returns a bitwise XOR of two numbers.
notes: Operates on 48-bit integers
pitfalls: Numbers are truncated to integers

name: BITLSHIFT
description_short: Shifts a number left by the specified number of bits.
notes: Equivalent to multiplying by 2^shift_amount
pitfalls: Can overflow for large shifts

name: BITRSHIFT
description_short: Shifts a number right by the specified number of bits.
notes: Equivalent to integer division by 2^shift_amount
pitfalls: Fractional results are truncated

name: COMBIN
description_short: Returns the number of combinations for a given number of items.
pitfalls: Both arguments must be non-negative integers

name: COMBINA
description_short: Returns the number of combinations with repetitions.
notes: Combinations with repetition allowed

name: PERMUT
description_short: Returns the number of permutations for a given number of items.

name: GEOMEAN
description_short: Returns the geometric mean of a column of positive numbers.
notes: All values must be positive
pitfalls: Returns error if any value is zero or negative

name: GEOMEANX
description_short: Returns the geometric mean of an expression evaluated for each row of a table.
notes: Iterator version of GEOMEAN
pitfalls: All evaluated values must be positive

name: LINEST
description_short: Returns a table of linear regression statistics for univariate data.
notes: Returns slope, intercept, and optionally R-squared
pitfalls: Requires numeric columns

name: LINESTX
description_short: Returns a table of linear regression statistics, evaluated for each row.
notes: Iterator version of LINEST

name: RANK.EQ
description_short: Returns the rank of a value in a column of numbers.
notes: Duplicate values get the same rank
pitfalls: Different from RANKX which evaluates expressions

name: ISAFTER
description_short: Returns TRUE if the first set of values is after the second set in the specified sort order.
notes: Supports multi-column comparison
pitfalls: Rarely used directly — mostly internal

name: ISONORAFTER
description_short: Returns TRUE if the first set of values is on or after the second set.
notes: Like ISAFTER but inclusive
pitfalls: Rarely used directly

name: COLUMNSTATISTICS
description_short: Returns a table of statistics about every column in every table in the model.
notes: Returns table name, column name, min, max, cardinality, max length
pitfalls: Only available in DAX queries, not measures

name: CUSTOMDATA
description_short: Returns the content of the CustomData connection string property.
notes: Used for passing custom parameters via connection strings
pitfalls: Not available in Power BI Desktop

name: ISINTEGER
description_short: Returns TRUE if a value is an integer.
notes: Checks if value has no decimal part
pitfalls: 1.0 may return TRUE or FALSE depending on storage

name: ISDATETIME
description_short: Returns TRUE if a value is a date/time.
notes: Checks column data type

name: ROLLUP
description_short: Modifies SUMMARIZE to add rollup (subtotal) rows for each group.
notes: Used inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS or SUMMARIZE
Adds subtotal/grand total rows
pitfalls: Only valid inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

name: ROLLUPADDISSUBTOTAL
description_short: Adds subtotal rows and an ISSUBTOTAL column to SUMMARIZECOLUMNS output.
notes: Used inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
Creates boolean column indicating subtotal rows
pitfalls: Only valid inside SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

name: ROLLUPISSUBTOTAL
description_short: Pairs a grouping column with an isSubtotal flag column in SUMMARIZECOLUMNS.
notes: Alternative to ROLLUPADDISSUBTOTAL
pitfalls: Requires pre-existing isSubtotal column

name: ROLLUPGROUP
description_short: Groups columns together in a ROLLUP so they are rolled up as a single unit.
notes: Used inside ROLLUP to prevent partial subtotals
pitfalls: Only valid inside ROLLUP within SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

name: YEARFRAC
description_short: Returns the fraction of the year between two dates.
notes: Basis 0: US 30/360, 1: Actual/Actual, 2: Actual/360, 3: Actual/365, 4: EU 30/360
pitfalls: Different bases give different results

name: NETWORKDAYS
description_short: Returns the number of working days between two dates.
notes: Excludes weekends and optional holidays
pitfalls: Weekend parameter uses specific encoding

name: BETA.DIST
description_short: Returns the beta distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

notes: Commonly used in project planning
pitfalls: Alpha and beta must be positive

name: BETA.INV
description_short: Returns the inverse of the beta cumulative distribution function.

name: CHISQ.DIST
description_short: Returns the chi-squared distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: CHISQ.DIST.RT
description_short: Returns the right-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution.

name: CHISQ.INV
description_short: Returns the inverse of the left-tailed chi-squared distribution.

name: CHISQ.INV.RT
description_short: Returns the inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution.

name: CONFIDENCE.NORM
description_short: Returns the confidence interval for a population mean using normal distribution.

name: CONFIDENCE.T
description_short: Returns the confidence interval using Student's t-distribution.
notes: Better for small samples

name: EXPON.DIST
description_short: Returns the exponential distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: NORM.DIST
description_short: Returns the normal distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: NORM.INV
description_short: Returns the inverse of the normal cumulative distribution.

name: NORM.S.DIST
description_short: Returns the standard normal distribution (mean=0, stdev=1).

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: NORM.S.INV
description_short: Returns the inverse of the standard normal cumulative distribution.
notes: Returns z-score for given probability

name: POISSON.DIST
description_short: Returns the Poisson distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: T.DIST
description_short: Returns the Student's t-distribution.

params.name: cumulative
params.description: TRUE for CDF, FALSE for PDF

name: T.DIST.2T
description_short: Returns the two-tailed Student's t-distribution.

name: T.DIST.RT
description_short: Returns the right-tailed Student's t-distribution.

name: T.INV
description_short: Returns the inverse of the left-tailed Student's t-distribution.

name: T.INV.2T
description_short: Returns the inverse of the two-tailed Student's t-distribution.

name: ACCRINT
description_short: Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays periodic interest.

name: ACCRINTM
description_short: Returns the accrued interest for a security that pays interest at maturity.

name: AMORDEGRC
description_short: Returns the depreciation for each accounting period (French accounting system, degressive).
notes: French accounting system

name: AMORLINC
description_short: Returns the depreciation for each accounting period (French accounting system, linear).
notes: French accounting linear method

name: CUMIPMT
description_short: Returns the cumulative interest paid on a loan between two periods.
pitfalls: Returns negative value

name: CUMPRINC
description_short: Returns the cumulative principal paid on a loan between two periods.
pitfalls: Returns negative value

name: DB
description_short: Returns the depreciation using the fixed-declining balance method.

name: DDB
description_short: Returns the depreciation using the double-declining balance method.

name: DISC
description_short: Returns the discount rate for a security.

name: DOLLARDE
description_short: Converts a price expressed as a fraction into a decimal.

name: DOLLARFR
description_short: Converts a decimal price into a fractional price.

name: DURATION
description_short: Returns the Macauley duration of a bond.

name: EFFECT
description_short: Returns the effective annual interest rate given nominal rate and compounding periods.

name: FV
description_short: Returns the future value of an investment.
pitfalls: Cash outflows are negative

name: INTRATE
description_short: Returns the interest rate for a fully invested security.

name: IPMT
description_short: Returns the interest payment for a given period of an investment.
pitfalls: Returns negative for outflows

name: ISPMT
description_short: Returns the interest paid during a specific period of an investment.
notes: Uses simple interest calculation

name: NOMINAL
description_short: Returns the nominal annual interest rate given the effective rate.
notes: Inverse of EFFECT

name: NPER
description_short: Returns the number of periods for an investment.

name: PDURATION
description_short: Returns the number of periods required for an investment to reach a specified value.
pitfalls: Rate must be positive

name: PMT
description_short: Returns the periodic payment for a loan or annuity.
notes: Returns negative for outflows
pitfalls: Monthly rate = annual rate / 12

name: PPMT
description_short: Returns the principal payment for a given period.

name: PV
description_short: Returns the present value of an investment.

name: RATE
description_short: Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity.
notes: Uses iterative calculation
pitfalls: May not converge

name: RECEIVED
description_short: Returns the amount received at maturity for a fully invested security.

name: RRI
description_short: Returns an equivalent interest rate for the growth of an investment.

name: SLN
description_short: Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period.
notes: Simple: (cost - salvage) / life

name: SYD
description_short: Returns the sum-of-years' digits depreciation for a specified period.

name: TBILLEQ
description_short: Returns the bond-equivalent yield for a Treasury bill.

name: TBILLPRICE
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value for a Treasury bill.

name: TBILLYIELD
description_short: Returns the yield for a Treasury bill.

name: VDB
description_short: Returns variable declining balance depreciation for any period.
notes: Most flexible depreciation function

name: XIRR
description_short: Returns the internal rate of return for a series of cash flows at irregular intervals.
notes: Dates need not be equally spaced
pitfalls: Must have at least one positive and one negative cash flow

name: XNPV
description_short: Returns the net present value for a series of cash flows at irregular intervals.
notes: Dates need not be equally spaced
pitfalls: Rate must be positive

name: YIELD
description_short: Returns the yield on a security that pays periodic interest.

name: YIELDDISC
description_short: Returns the annual yield for a discounted security.

name: YIELDMAT
description_short: Returns the annual yield for a security that pays interest at maturity.

name: PRICE
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value of a security that pays periodic interest.

name: PRICEDISC
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value of a discounted security.

name: PRICEMAT
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value for a security that pays interest at maturity.

name: MDURATION
description_short: Returns the modified Macauley duration of a bond.
notes: MDURATION = DURATION / (1 + yld/frequency)

name: COUPDAYBS
description_short: Returns the number of days from the beginning of the coupon period to the settlement date.

name: COUPDAYS
description_short: Returns the number of days in the coupon period that contains the settlement date.

name: COUPDAYSNC
description_short: Returns the number of days from the settlement date to the next coupon date.

name: COUPNCD
description_short: Returns the next coupon date after the settlement date.

name: COUPNUM
description_short: Returns the number of coupons payable between the settlement and maturity dates.

name: COUPPCD
description_short: Returns the previous coupon date before the settlement date.

name: ODDFPRICE
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value for a security with an odd first period.

name: ODDFYIELD
description_short: Returns the yield of a security with an odd first period.

name: ODDLPRICE
description_short: Returns the price per $100 face value for a security with an odd last period.

name: ODDLYIELD
description_short: Returns the yield of a security with an odd last period.
